messages:
anna_marketing: hey @sam_runtime @devon_eng — we need a compact artifact + method note to back a pressline for next Tue. Headline: \"~2.5x lower per-token cost on X when using 4-bit quant + batching\". Can you run a focused smoke to validate?

sam_runtime: quick q: which model variant exactly? and what's the target prompt length distribution? will affect batching/kernels.

anna_marketing: target = open-model-x-v2 (context 2k). cohort = short (avg 32 tokens), medium (128), long (512). priority = high for marketing launch.

sam_runtime: ok. we'll measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, coldstart vs warmed, throughput at conc 1/5/10, and token-level cost. Also want quant-4 vs fp16 comparison. any required eval prompts or golden outputs?

anna_marketing: yes please include 10 sample traces per cohort (we'll run evals). need raw logs + reproducible payloads + runbook. also a short plain-language method blurb we can paste into the press packet.

devon_eng: will do. suggested warmup: 50 short warmup requests then 10 medium, 5 long, then baseline runs. quantized runs may need extra kernel warmup. sample payload below — use seed=42 and the same RNG across runs:

```
{"input": "Summarize the following product feature in 2-3 sentences: Redwood Inference reduces per-token inference cost by smart batching and quantization.", "max_tokens": 120, "temperature": 0.0, "seed": 42}
```

devon_eng: run configs: 3 repeats per test, report mean+stddev, and export per-request csv with columns: request_id, cohort, seq_len, latency_ms, tokens_out, model_variant, quant_mode.

sam_runtime: noted. we'll also produce a heatmap of tail latency across concurrent clients and a coldstart timeline (first token latency over time).

ci-bot: scheduled job created: https://ci.internal/runs/1788884321-smoke (small warmup -> 3x sweep). started at 1788884400.

marco_product: tagging product — marketing needs final artifact by Mon 10am PT for press review. can runtime make that deadline? :eyes:

sam_runtime: monday 9am PT deliverable is tight but feasible if we parallelize quant and fp16 runs. quant tuning might add ~2h. can we push final approval to Mon EOD if tuning causes delay?

anna_marketing: press insists on Mon morning. if tuning pushes, we will label quant numbers as \"pre-tuning\" and include caveats. still want best-effort tuning though.

lisa_pm: note — include a short bullet list of caveats: workload dependent, batch size assumptions, cost model used (GPU-hours + infra overhead), and versioned model id.

devon_eng: will include a minimal runbook (steps, commands, config) and a small reproduce script. we'll upload artifacts to S3 and post link in thread. sample command: 

```
./run_smoke.sh --model open-model-x-v2 --quant 4 --cohorts short,medium,long --repeats 3 --seed 42 --out /tmp/bench-1788884321
```

sam_runtime: will post preliminary numbers as soon as the CI run finishes. ping me here if we need to escalate.

anna_marketing: big thanks — please call out which numbers are smokes vs fully tuned. marketing will craft copy to reflect uncertainty. :pray: 

ci-bot: smoke job completed. artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/bench/1788884321/smoke.tar.gz — contains csvs + sample traces + logs.

sam_runtime: uploaded tuned fp16 runs. quant-4 runs are pre-tuning (kernel warmups pending). link: s3://redwood-artifacts/bench/1788884321/fp16_tuned/

devon_eng: prepping quant tuning; ETA 3 hours. i'll post final artifacts and a 2-paragraph method blurb once done.

anna_marketing: perfect. once you post the final artifacts i'll draft the pressline and send for legal. thanks team! :tada:
